question: ______ is the only continent through which the tropic of cancer, the equator and the tropic of capricorn passes.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Africa.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Africa is the only continent through which all three major latitude lines — the Tropic of Cancer, the Equator, and the Tropic of Capricorn — pass. (अफ्रीका महाद्वीप — कर्क रेखा, भूमध्य रेखा और मकर रेखा)

 

• The Tropic of Cancer (23.5°N) passes through northern Africa, including Algeria, Libya, Egypt, Niger and Mali.

 

• The Equator (0°) passes through central Africa, including Kenya, Uganda, Gabon and the DR Congo.

 

• The Tropic of Capricorn (23.5°S) passes through southern Africa, including Namibia, Botswana, South Africa and Mozambique.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• South America is crossed by the Equator and the Tropic of Capricorn, but not the Tropic of Cancer.

 

• Asia is crossed by the Tropic of Cancer, but not the Equator or the Tropic of Capricorn.

 

NOTE

 

• North America (Option 1): Crossed by the Tropic of Cancer only.

 

• Europe (Option 3): Not crossed by any of the three lines.

 

• Asia (Option 4): Crossed by the Tropic of Cancer only; the Equator and Tropic of Capricorn do not pass through it.

question: Which of the following is NOT correct about the jurisdiction of the High Court?
option_1: It controls the subordinate courts within its jurisdiction.
option_2: It has the power of judicial review.
option_3: It provides advisory opinion to the President of India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is It provides advisory opinion to the President of India.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The power to give an advisory opinion to the President of India on questions of law or fact belongs to the Supreme Court under Article 143, not to the High Court. (राष्ट्रपति को परामर्शी राय — अनुच्छेद 143, उच्चतम न्यायालय)

 

• A High Court exercises superintendence over subordinate courts within its territorial jurisdiction under Article 227.

 

• It also exercises the power of judicial review, examining the constitutional validity of laws and executive actions.

 

• Under Article 226, a High Court has writ jurisdiction — it can issue writs (habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, certiorari, quo warranto) not only for enforcement of Fundamental Rights but also for 'any other purpose', making its writ jurisdiction wider than that of the Supreme Court under Article 32.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• High Courts are established under Article 214 of the Constitution; India currently has 25 High Courts.

 

• The Chief Justice of a High Court is appointed by the President of India in consultation with the CJI and the Governor of the state.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (subordinate courts): This is a correct power of the High Court (Article 227), so it is not the answer.

 

• Option 2 (judicial review): This is a correct power of the High Court, so it is not the answer.

 

• Option 4 (writ jurisdiction): This is a correct power of the High Court (Article 226), so it is not the answer.

question: Who released a special stamp entitled ‘Wheat Revolution’ in July 1968?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Indira Gandhi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In July 1968, Prime Minister Indira Gandhi released a special commemorative postage stamp titled 'Wheat Revolution' to mark India's dramatic rise in wheat production. (गेहूं क्रांति डाक टिकट — इंदिरा गांधी)

 

• The stamp celebrated the success of the Green Revolution, driven by high-yielding wheat varieties developed with agricultural scientist Norman Borlaug's dwarf wheat strains and championed in India by M.S. Swaminathan.

 

• Indira Gandhi served as Prime Minister of India from 1966 to 1977 and again from 1980 to 1984, making her the sitting PM in 1968.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Green Revolution in India began in the mid-1960s and was concentrated in Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh.

 

• C. Subramaniam, Union Agriculture Minister (1964-66), is widely regarded as an architect of India's Green Revolution.

 

NOTE

 

• Mahatma Gandhi (Option 1): Assassinated in 1948, two decades before this event; could not have released the stamp.

 

• Jawaharlal Nehru (Option 2): Died in 1964, before the stamp was released in 1968.

 

• Motilal Nehru (Option 4): Died in 1931, long before this event.

question: Who among the following ruled in India between 1266 and 1287?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ghiyasuddin Balban.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ghiyasuddin Balban ruled the Delhi Sultanate from 1266 to 1287 CE as a ruler of the Mamluk (Slave) dynasty. (बलबन — 1266-1287)

 

• He introduced strict court discipline and ceremonies such as sijda (prostration) and paibos (kissing the ruler's feet), and propagated the 'Theory of Kingship', styling himself Zil-i-Ilahi ('Shadow of God on Earth').

 

• He crushed the powerful group of nobles known as the 'Chahalgani' (Group/Corps of Forty) to consolidate royal authority.

 

• He strengthened the espionage (barid) system and reorganised the military department (Diwan-i-Arz) to defend against Mongol invasions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Balban was succeeded by his grandson Kaiqubad; the Slave dynasty ended in 1290 when Jalaluddin Khilji founded the Khilji dynasty.

 

• Balban began his career as one of the 'Chihalgani' nobles himself, under Iltutmish, before rising to the throne.

 

NOTE

 

• Qutub-ud-din Aybak (Option 1): Founder of the Slave dynasty, ruled 1206-1210.

 

• Aram Shah (Option 2): A short-lived, weak successor of Aybak who ruled briefly around 1210-1211.

 

• Shams-ud-din Iltutmish (Option 3): Ruled from 1211 to 1236, well before the given period.

question: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a Fundamental Right in the Constitution of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Right to property.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Right to Property was originally a Fundamental Right under Article 31, but it was removed from the list of Fundamental Rights by the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978, and made a mere legal right under Article 300A. (संपत्ति का अधिकार — 44वां संविधान संशोधन, 1978)

 

• The Constitution currently guarantees six Fundamental Rights: Right to Equality, Right to Freedom, Right against Exploitation, Right to Freedom of Religion, Cultural and Educational Rights, and Right to Constitutional Remedies.

 

• The Right to Education was made a Fundamental Right under Article 21A by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Originally, the Constitution provided for seven Fundamental Rights (including Right to Property); this was reduced to six after 1978.

 

• Fundamental Rights are enshrined in Part III of the Constitution, often called the 'Magna Carta' of India.

 

NOTE

 

• Right to education (Option 1): A Fundamental Right under Article 21A, so it is not the answer.

 

• Right to freedom (Option 3): A Fundamental Right under Articles 19-22, so it is not the answer.

 

• Right against exploitation (Option 4): A Fundamental Right under Articles 23-24, so it is not the answer.

question: In February 2022, Maharashtra government announced ‘Hope Express’ initiative to _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is prevent cancer.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In February 2022, the Maharashtra government, through its Health Minister, launched the 'Hope Express' initiative to spread awareness about cancer prevention, early detection and screening. (होप एक्सप्रेस — कैंसर की रोकथाम)

 

• The initiative was timed around World Cancer Day (4 February) and was aimed at taking screening and awareness camps to rural and tribal parts of the state.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• World Cancer Day is observed globally every year on 4 February to raise cancer awareness and encourage prevention, detection and treatment.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 2, 3 and 4 (drainage, industrial waste, air quality) describe unrelated civic/environmental issues, not the actual purpose of the 'Hope Express' initiative.

question: Who among the following was awarded the National Nritya Shiromani Award 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Aparna Satheesan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Aparna Satheesan, a classical dancer, was conferred the National Nritya Shiromani Award 2022 in recognition of her contribution to classical dance. (राष्ट्रीय नृत्य शिरोमणि पुरस्कार — अपर्णा सतीशन)

 

• The award recognises excellence and lifetime contribution in the field of Indian classical dance forms.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's classical dance traditions include Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam, Kathakali and Sattriya, each recognised by the Sangeet Natak Akademi.

 

NOTE

 

• Radha Reddy (Option 1), Usha Srinivasan (Option 3) and Deepa Sashindran (Option 4): None of them were the recipients of the National Nritya Shiromani Award 2022.

question: Which food requires a longer small intestine to digest food?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Grass.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Plant material such as grass is rich in cellulose, a complex carbohydrate that is difficult to break down, so herbivorous diets require a longer small intestine (and often a larger caecum) to allow more time and surface area for digestion and nutrient absorption. (घास — शाकाहारी भोजन, लंबी छोटी आंत)

 

• In contrast, animal-based/protein-rich foods such as meat and eggs are digested relatively quickly and completely, so carnivores typically have a shorter small intestine relative to body length.

 

• This is a general biological principle seen across the animal kingdom — herbivores (long intestine) vs carnivores (short intestine), with omnivores falling in between.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Herbivores like cattle and sheep also rely on gut microbes/symbiotic bacteria (and in ruminants, a specialised four-chambered stomach) to help break down cellulose, which grass digestion additionally depends on.

 

NOTE

 

• Lamb (Option 1), Eggs (Option 2) and Chicken (Option 4): These are animal-protein-based foods, which digest faster and require a comparatively shorter small intestine than fibrous plant material like grass.

question: Yellow card in badminton indicates:
solution_text:
The correct answer is warning for misconduct.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In badminton, the umpire follows a graded code-of-conduct system using coloured cards. A yellow card is shown as a warning for misconduct — the first and mildest level of sanction. (पीला कार्ड — बैडमिंटन में चेतावनी)

 

• If misconduct continues after a yellow card, the umpire shows a red card, which awards a fault (point) to the opponent.

 

• For the most serious misconduct, the umpire shows a black card, leading to disqualification of the player from the match/tournament.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Badminton World Federation (BWF) governs the sport's rules, including the Player's Code of Conduct that defines this card system.

 

NOTE

 

• Fault for misconduct (Option 1): This corresponds to a red card, not a yellow card.

 

• Suspension for misconduct (Option 2): Not a recognised badminton card sanction.

 

• Disqualified for misconduct (Option 4): This corresponds to a black card, not a yellow card.

question: The national Archives of India came up in the ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1920s.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The National Archives of India (NAI) traces its origin to the Imperial Record Department, set up in Calcutta in March 1891; it was shifted to the new capital and its present building in New Delhi came up in the 1920s, with the institution taking its recognisable modern form in that decade. (राष्ट्रीय अभिलेखागार — 1920 का दशक)

 

• It was renamed the National Archives of India after independence in 1947.

 

• It functions under the Ministry of Culture, Government of India, and holds non-current records of the Government of India along with private archives of national importance.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• NAI is located on Janpath, New Delhi, close to India Gate, and is the custodian of some of the country's most valuable historical records, including originals of the Constitution of India-related documents.

 

NOTE

 

• 1930s (Option 1), 1910s (Option 2) and 1900s (Option 4): These decades do not correspond to when the National Archives of India came up in its present form.

question: Personal disposable income (PDI) can be defined as ________.
option_2: PI + Personal tax payments – Non-tax payments
option_3: PI – Personal tax payments – Non-tax payments
option_4: PI – Personal tax payments + Non-tax payments
solution_text:
The correct answer is PI – Personal tax payments – Non-tax payments.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Personal Disposable Income (PDI) is the income that actually remains with individuals/households for consumption or saving after all taxes and other compulsory non-tax payments are deducted from Personal Income (PI). (व्यक्तिगत प्रयोज्य आय — PI घटा कर एवं गैर-कर भुगतान)

 

• Formula: PDI = Personal Income (PI) – Personal tax payments – Non-tax payments (such as fines, fees, and other miscellaneous payments to the government).

 

• PDI represents the income households are free to either spend (consumption) or save, i.e., PDI = Consumption Expenditure + Personal Saving.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Personal Income (PI) itself is derived from National Income by adjusting for undistributed profits, corporate taxes, social security contributions, and adding transfer payments.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 4: Each uses an incorrect sign combination (addition instead of subtraction for tax/non-tax payments), which does not match the correct formula for PDI.

question: In India the 1st census was held in the year ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1872.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The first census in India was conducted in 1872, during the tenure of Governor-General Lord Mayo, though it was not conducted simultaneously across the entire country. (भारत की प्रथम जनगणना — 1872)

 

• The first synchronous (i.e., conducted at the same time all over the country) census was held in 1881 under Lord Ripon.

 

• Since 1881, a census has been conducted every 10 years without interruption (the 2021 census was postponed due to the COVID-19 pandemic).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Census-taking in independent India is conducted under the Census Act, 1948, by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India.

 

NOTE

 

• 1860 (Option 2), 1900 (Option 3) and 1920 (Option 4): None of these correspond to the year of India's first census.

question: The Kunbi dance is performed by the tribal community of ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Goa.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Kunbi dance is a traditional folk dance performed by the Kunbi tribal community of Goa. (कुनबी नृत्य — गोवा)

 

• It is typically performed by Kunbi women wearing the traditional short 'Kunbi saree' (Kapod/Kapad), and is closely associated with harvest celebrations.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other well-known folk dances of Goa include Fugdi, Dhalo, Dekhni and Mando.

 

NOTE

 

• Sikkim (Option 1), Tamil Nadu (Option 2) and Uttar Pradesh (Option 3): The Kunbi dance is not native to these states; it is specifically associated with Goa.

question: A cyclone is known by different names in different parts of the world. In Philippines it is called as ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is typhoon.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A tropical cyclone is called a 'typhoon' in the Philippines, Japan, China and the North-West Pacific region. (टाइफून — फिलीपींस में चक्रवात)

 

• It is called a 'hurricane' in the Atlantic Ocean and North-East Pacific (e.g. USA, Caribbean).

 

• It is called a 'willy-willy' (an older/informal term) in Australia, and simply a 'cyclone' in the Indian Ocean/Bay of Bengal/Arabian Sea region.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• 'Mango shower' refers to pre-monsoon rain showers in South India (associated with ripening mangoes), and is unrelated to cyclone terminology.

 

NOTE

 

• willy-willy (Option 1): Australian term for a tropical cyclone, not used in the Philippines.

 

• hurricane (Option 2): Used in the Atlantic/North-East Pacific region, not the Philippines.

 

• mango shower (Option 4): An unrelated meteorological term for pre-monsoon rains, not a name for a cyclone.

question: Who among the following defeated Mughal emperor Humayun at Chausa?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sher Khan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sher Khan (later known as Sher Shah Suri) defeated the Mughal emperor Humayun at the Battle of Chausa in 1539. (शेरशाह सूरी — चौसा का युद्ध, 1539)

 

• He decisively defeated Humayun again at the Battle of Kannauj (Bilgram) in 1540, forcing Humayun into exile and establishing the Sur Empire.

 

• Sher Shah Suri is remembered for major administrative reforms, including the construction of the Grand Trunk (Sadak-e-Azam) Road and introducing the currency 'Rupiya'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Humayun regained the Mughal throne in 1555 after the decline of the Sur dynasty following Sher Shah's death in 1545.

 

NOTE

 

• Mirza Hakim (Option 1) and Mirza Kamran (Option 4): Both were Humayun's own brothers/relatives, not involved in the Battle of Chausa.

 

• Safavid Shah (Option 2): Refers to the ruler of Persia (Shah Tahmasp), who later gave refuge to Humayun during his exile, but was not involved in the Battle of Chausa.

question: Prime Minister Narendra Modi said, “Seema Darshan Project adds a new dimension to the tourism sector”. This project will boost tourism in _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gujarat.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Seema Darshan Project is located at Nadabet, in the Banaskantha district of Gujarat, along the India-Pakistan border. (सीमा दर्शन परियोजना — नाडाबेट, गुजरात)

 

• It allows tourists to visit the border area, watch the Border Security Force (BSF) in action, and witness a retreat ceremony, similar in spirit to the Wagah border ceremony.

 

• Prime Minister Narendra Modi referred to this project as adding a new dimension to border tourism in the state.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Nadabet is developed and maintained jointly by the BSF and the Gujarat Tourism department as part of efforts to promote border tourism.

 

NOTE

 

• Uttar Pradesh (Option 2), Rajasthan (Option 3) and Jammu and Kashmir (Option 4): The Seema Darshan Project referenced here is specific to Gujarat, not these states.

question: ______ has become the first city in the country to get a processed steel slag (industrial waste) road.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Surat.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Surat, Gujarat, became the first city in India to get a road built using processed steel slag (a solid waste generated from steel plants). (सूरत — भारत की पहली स्टील स्लैग रोड)

 

• The road was developed by AM/NS India (ArcelorMittal Nippon Steel India) in collaboration with CSIR-CRRI (Central Road Research Institute) and the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI), and was inaugurated in April 2022.

 

• Steel slag roads are considered more durable than conventional roads and support the 'waste-to-wealth' approach by recycling industrial by-products.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The steel slag road project is aligned with India's push toward sustainable infrastructure and reducing industrial waste disposal burden.

 

NOTE

 

• Chennai (Option 2), Kanpur (Option 3) and Shimla (Option 4): None of these cities got India's first processed steel slag road; that distinction belongs to Surat.

question: Which country hosted the first ever Commonwealth Games in 1930?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Canada.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The first edition of the Games (then called the British Empire Games, the precursor of the Commonwealth Games) was held in 1930 in Hamilton, Ontario, Canada. (राष्ट्रमंडल खेल — 1930, कनाडा)

 

• The event was later renamed the British Empire and Commonwealth Games, then the British Commonwealth Games, and finally the Commonwealth Games in 1978.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India first participated in the Commonwealth Games at the 1934 London edition.

 

• The Commonwealth Games are held every four years, involving athletes from Commonwealth nations.

 

NOTE

 

• Australia (Option 1), New Zealand (Option 2) and England (Option 3): All have hosted the Commonwealth Games in later years, but none hosted the inaugural 1930 edition.

question: The theory of plate tectonics proposes that the earth’s lithosphere is divided into ______ major and some minor plates.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 7.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• According to the theory of plate tectonics, the Earth's lithosphere is divided into 7 major plates — the Pacific, North American, South American, Eurasian, African, Indo-Australian and Antarctic plates — along with several minor plates. (प्लेट विवर्तनिकी सिद्धांत — 7 प्रमुख प्लेटें)

 

• These rigid plates float over the semi-fluid asthenosphere and their relative movement (convergent, divergent, and transform boundaries) causes earthquakes, volcanic activity, and mountain building.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Important minor plates include the Nazca, Cocos, Arabian, Caribbean, Philippine, Juan de Fuca and Scotia plates.

 

NOTE

 

• 6 (Option 2), 12 (Option 3) and 16 (Option 4): These numbers do not match the widely accepted count of 7 major tectonic plates.

question: Why does one get cramps after sudden physical activity?
option_1: The build-up of hydrochloric acid in our muscles during sudden activity causes cramps.
option_2: The pepsin enzyme releases chemicals that lead to cramps.
option_4: The build-up of lactic acid in our muscles during sudden activity causes cramps.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The build-up of lactic acid in our muscles during sudden activity causes cramps.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• During sudden or intense physical activity, the oxygen supply to muscles becomes insufficient, forcing muscle cells to respire anaerobically, which produces lactic acid. (लैक्टिक एसिड — मांसपेशियों में ऐंठन)

 

• The build-up of this lactic acid in the muscles is the standard textbook explanation for the fatigue and painful cramps experienced after strenuous exertion.

 

• This process (anaerobic respiration/glycolysis without sufficient oxygen) is distinct from normal aerobic respiration, which does not produce a lactic acid build-up.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Hydrochloric acid (HCl) and pepsin are digestive substances secreted in the stomach, unrelated to muscular activity or cramps.

 

NOTE

 

• Hydrochloric acid build-up (Option 1): HCl is a stomach digestive secretion, not linked to muscle cramps.

 

• Pepsin enzyme (Option 2): Pepsin is a digestive enzyme active in the stomach, unrelated to muscular cramping.

 

• Oxygen molecules breaking down (Option 3): This is not a recognised physiological cause of muscle cramps.

question:
Match the elements in column A with the element group they belong to, in column B.

Column-A (Element): i. Na    ii. Cu    iii. Mg    iv. He

Column-B (Group of element in the periodic table): a. Alkali metal    b. Alkaline earth metal    c. Transition metal    d. Zero group element
solution_text:
The correct answer is i-a, ii-c, iii-b, iv-d.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sodium (Na) belongs to Group 1 and is an alkali metal (i-a). (सोडियम — क्षार धातु)

 

• Copper (Cu) is a d-block element and is a transition metal (ii-c).

 

• Magnesium (Mg) belongs to Group 2 and is an alkaline earth metal (iii-b).

 

• Helium (He) belongs to Group 18 and is a zero group element / noble gas (iv-d).

 

• Putting these together gives the correct matching: i-a, ii-c, iii-b, iv-d.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Zero group elements (also called Group 18 or noble gases) include Helium, Neon, Argon, Krypton, Xenon and Radon, all characterised by complete outer electron shells and very low reactivity.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (i-a, ii-d, iii-b, iv-c): Incorrectly places Copper in the zero group and Helium as a transition metal.

 

• Option 2 (i-a, ii-b, iii-c, iv-d): Incorrectly places Copper as an alkaline earth metal and Magnesium as a transition metal.

 

• Option 4 (i-d, ii-a, iii-b, iv-c): Incorrectly places Sodium in the zero group and Copper as an alkali metal.

question: Abdul Karim Khan and Abdul Wahid Khan were the founders of the ________ gharana.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kirana.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Abdul Karim Khan and Abdul Wahid Khan are credited as the founders of the Kirana Gharana of Hindustani classical vocal music. (किराना घराना — अब्दुल करीम खान)

 

• The gharana is named after Kirana, a small town in Uttar Pradesh, and is known for its emphasis on swara (note) purity and slow, meditative elaboration of the raga (bol banana).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Famous exponents of the Kirana Gharana include Pt. Bhimsen Joshi and Gangubai Hangal.

 

NOTE

 

• Jaipur-Atrauli (Option 1): Founded by Ustad Alladiya Khan.

 

• Gwalior (Option 2): The oldest of the khyal gharanas, associated with the Haddu Khan-Hassu Khan lineage.

 

• Agra (Option 3): Founded by Ghagge Khuda Baksh.

question: Who among the following has the credit to invent and create a new style of ‘Bharatanatyam’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dr Padma Subrahmanyam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dr. Padma Subrahmanyam is credited with inventing and creating a new dance style, 'Bharatanrityam', developed from Bharatanatyam through her extensive research on Bharata's Natya Shastra and the 108 karanas (sculptural dance poses) described in ancient texts and temple sculptures. (पद्मा सुब्रह्मण्यम — भरतनृत्यम शैली)

 

• She is a scholar-dancer and recipient of both the Padma Shri and Padma Bhushan for her contributions to Indian classical dance.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Rukmini Devi Arundale is renowned as the reviver and reformer of Bharatanatyam — she removed its association with the Devadasi tradition and founded Kalakshetra in 1936 — but she is credited with reviving/reforming the existing form, not inventing a wholly new style.

 

NOTE

 

• Yamini Krishnamurthy (Option 1): A renowned Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi dancer, but not credited with creating a new style.

 

• Rukmini Devi Arundale (Option 3): Credited with reviving and reforming Bharatanatyam and founding Kalakshetra, not with inventing a new style.

 

• Chinta Ravi Bala Krishna (Option 4): Not associated with creating a new style of Bharatanatyam.

question: Puhar or Kaveripattinam, was the port of which of the following dynasty?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cholas.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Puhar, also known as Kaveripattinam (Poompuhar), was the chief port and an early capital of the Chola dynasty, situated at the mouth of the Kaveri river in present-day Tamil Nadu. (कावेरीपट्टिनम/पुहार — चोल वंश का बंदरगाह)

 

• It is mentioned as a flourishing centre of trade in Sangam literature, notably in the epic Silappadikaram.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Later Chola capitals included Thanjavur and Gangaikonda Cholapuram, established under rulers like Rajaraja I and Rajendra I.

 

NOTE

 

• Cheras (Option 1): Their chief port was Muziris, with capitals at Vanchi/Karur.

 

• Pandyas (Option 3): Their chief port was Korkai, with capital at Madurai.

 

• Vakatakas (Option 4): A dynasty of central India (the Deccan), unrelated to this Tamil coastal port.

question: National Dairy Research Institute is located at:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Karnal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The National Dairy Research Institute (NDRI) is located at Karnal, Haryana. (राष्ट्रीय डेयरी अनुसंधान संस्थान — करनाल)

 

• It is a premier deemed university under the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), dedicated to dairy research, education and extension.

 

• NDRI was originally established in 1923 in Bangalore and later shifted to Karnal in 1955.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• NDRI, Karnal, is known for developing improved cattle breeds such as 'Karan Fries' and 'Karan Swiss'.

 

NOTE

 

• Anand (Option 2): Home to the National Dairy Development Board (NDDB) and IRMA, not NDRI.

 

• Lucknow (Option 3): Not associated with NDRI.

 

• Palampur (Option 4): Home to CSK Himachal Pradesh Krishi Vishvavidyalaya, not NDRI.
